title: Sharp Football Analysis Review 2026: Price, Record, Worth It?
description: Sharp Football Analysis review, checked 7 Nov 2026: Warren Sharp package prices, the no refund policy, what his records leave out and what buyers say.
dek: Warren Sharp sells NFL and college football betting picks, props, futures and fantasy content, from $29.99 a week to $899 a season, with no refunds. The site posts yearly win and loss totals going back to 2006, but every record we could open is kept and published by the seller.

status.label: Not verified
status.note: Watchdog has not graded a full, time stamped record of Warren Sharp's picks. This page reports what we could check and labels everything else.

glance: Sharp Football Analysis, LLC (site footer). The app seller is listed as Sharp Football Holdings, LLC
None found. Refund policy says no refunds
Not found. Yearly and season totals only
short_answer: Sharp Football Analysis is a real, well known business. It names the company that runs it, publishes its prices, and Warren Sharp's football analysis and books are widely read. In that sense it is legitimate.

Whether the picks make money for a buyer is a separate question. The site shows yearly records such as "1,781-1,295 (58%) +391.6 Units" since 2006 and "739-431 (63%)" on computer totals, but these are the seller's own totals. We found no outside party that keeps or audits the picks, and no public log of every pick with the line and release time on the pages we could open without paying.
Treat the records as seller marketing until you can check them. If you buy, start with a week, save every pick with the line you could actually get, and remember the policy says no refunds.
pricing_intro: Prices below were shown on the Sharp Football Analysis package pages on 7 Nov 2026. Season prices are one time payments; weekly and 4 week plans were labeled billed weekly or billed monthly. Where a page showed a struck price and a sale price, we list both.
pricing: 4 weeks $34.99 · draft kit $29.99 · draft kit plus season bundle $150 (listed as $189.99). The page showed two different full season prices, $99.99 and $159.99
guarantee: There is no guarantee. We found no promise of a free extension, credit or refund on any package page we opened. The cancelation and refund policy says buyers are acquiring electronic information delivered at purchase, and "No refunds will be processed on account of this fact."

Weekly and monthly plans can be cancelled at any time, but the policy says access to the dashboard and active recommendations is revoked immediately when you cancel, so you lose the rest of the period you paid for. The same page says sharing the picks gets an account closed with no refund. The policy page still refers to a 2025 subscription in places, so it may not have been fully updated for 2026. The terms of service also send disputes to binding arbitration and waive class actions.

claims_note: The dollar figures need reading closely. The NFL Plus page explains that the 2026 total is +14.24 units on "a standard bet size of 0.5 units," and that this is how "a $100 bettor was up $2,848." In other words, the "$100 bettor" bets $100 per standard play, which is $200 per unit, so the dollar figure is twice what +14.24 units would be at $100 a unit.

The site shows two different NFL records for the same year. The lifetime page lists NFL "all releases" for 2025 as 63-49, and the same page lists "NFL Overall: 500-374" for the final 2025 package record. The pages we read do not explain what each count includes. Smaller numbers also drift between pages: computer totals over the last 6 years are 150-71 on two package pages and 145-71 on the NFL Plus page, the 2026 best bet record of 5-3 is shown as 57% on one page and 63% on another, and the book is described as 400+ pages on one page and 600+ pages on another.
record: What a buyer can verify independently: nothing we could find. We found no full, time stamped log of every pick kept by an outside party, no contest results run by a third party, and no regulator or court record about the records.

What the seller publishes: yearly win and loss totals for NFL picks back to 2016 plus a lifetime total since 2006, yearly computer totals records, final package records for 2021 to 2025, and a running 2026 record through week 8. The site says active picks are shown only to logged in members. On the free pages we opened we did not find a list of each past pick with the line, the price and the time it was sent, so a buyer cannot check whether every pick is counted or how the totals were graded.

What the seller's own numbers say: a 58% lifetime NFL record at about +391.6 units is a modest edge if it is complete and accurate, and it depends on getting the posted lines. The site itself says the picks move the market when released, which means a buyer who bets later may get a worse number than the one in the record.

our_data.text: Watchdog grades picks captured from public posts before the game starts. In this edition no Sharp Football Analysis pick feed is matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about how Warren Sharp's picks perform.
our_data.context: For scale: the site advertises a 63% lifetime record on computer totals. On the Watchdog board on 7 Nov 2026, {{over60}} of {{established}} established accounts (100 or more graded picks) were at 60% or better, and the median established account won {{median_win}}% of its picks. At standard -110 odds a bettor needs about 52.4% to break even.

customers_intro: Independent customer evidence on Sharp Football Analysis is thin and split. Trustpilot has six reviews, half five stars and half one star, the App Store has seven ratings, and the testimonials on the site are chosen by the seller. Below is everything we found and how much weight it can carry.

customers.text: The site's "Is Warren Sharp Legit?" page quotes subscribers from its own end of season surveys and says the quotes are unedited. All quoted comments are positive. The seller chose which ones to publish, so they cannot tell you what a typical buyer experiences.

Two recent Trustpilot reviewers were happy. One said he had been a customer for five NFL seasons and won each year and liked the app; another said he had bought the betting picks for three seasons and was pleased with the results. Neither posted a record.

A Trustpilot reviewer said a $5 seven day trial turned into $99 a week, that the picks were bad, and that cancelling was hard because the phone number and the website steps did not work, so he had to email. We did not see a $5 trial on the site on 7 Nov 2026.

A Trustpilot reviewer called it a legitimate service but said the picks lost for weeks while he paid over $100 a week, and that the plays leaned heavily on overs. He posted no log. A Jan 2020 reviewer pointed to an outside account's tally of a losing 2019 season; we did not open or verify that tally.
A Trustpilot reviewer said one week of NFL props went 7-3, including 4-1 on larger plays. One week is not a sample.

On the App Store, the Sharp Football alerts app had 4.4 out of 5 from 7 ratings on 7 Nov 2026. The one review shown praised push alerts that arrive faster than the old text messages. It says nothing about results.

In a TheRX thread about Warren Sharp's 2021 preview book, one member said the data is often framed to fit his conclusions and guessed that records may use lines no longer available, with no evidence. Another said his record had declined after a strong run years earlier, that his totals were his strength at around 60%, and that the college picks were worse. Neither posted figures we could check.

Reddit blocked our access, so we could not read any Reddit discussion. We found no Better Business Bureau profile we could confirm, and no court case or regulator action about Warren Sharp or Sharp Football Analysis in our searches.

conflicts: The site earns from betting operators. Its terms say the site "may feature advertisements (including affiliate or referral links) for sports betting or gambling operators from whom we may receive compensation." On 7 Nov 2026 the homepage linked articles for a Caesars promo code, a bet365 bonus code, DraftKings promotions and sportsbook bonus roundups, plus a Kalshi promo code page using the code WSHARP and a Polymarket referral code. That does not prove anything about the picks, but it is a financial interest a buyer should know about.
The paid packages and the free articles live on the same site as these promotions, so read free picks there knowing the site may be paid when readers sign up with a book.
strengths: A named company, published prices for every package and written refund and cancelation rules.
The site publishes yearly records, including weak numbers such as a 2018 NFL record of 67-64 and a 2026 computer totals record of 6-6, which is more than many sellers show.
Warren Sharp's analysis, articles and podcasts are free to read, so a buyer can judge the thinking before paying, and weekly plans keep the first purchase small.
concerns: No outside audit and no public pick by pick log on the pages we could open. Every record is kept by the seller.
No refunds, and cancelling a plan cuts off access at once.
Some record figures conflict between pages, and the "$100 bettor" dollar totals count $200 per unit.
The site carries sportsbook and prediction market promo codes that can pay the site.
Customer evidence is small and split, with complaints about losing stretches and cancelling.
checklist: Ask for every pick from the last 12 months with the line, the odds and the time it was sent. A list of hot runs is not a record.
Count units, not wins. A 60% record at heavy favorites can still lose money.
Read the guarantee for the words refund, credit and extension. Most "guarantees" in this business are credits.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get.
Give any handicapper a few hundred picks before you call them a winner. Short runs swing hard both ways.
faq: It is a real business, Sharp Football Analysis, LLC, run by Warren Sharp, with published prices and a long public body of football analysis. We could not verify that its picks win over time, because the records are kept and published only by the seller.
How much does Sharp Football Analysis cost?

On 7 Nov 2026 betting packages ran from $79.99 to $109.99 a week, $249.99 to $329.99 for 4 weeks, and $399.99 to $899 for a season, depending on the package. College props started at $29.99 a week, NFL props were $599.99 a season, and the policy says no refunds.
Does Sharp Football Analysis have a verified record?

Not independently. The site posts yearly records back to 2006, including a lifetime NFL claim of 1,781-1,295 (58%), but no outside party keeps or audits them, we found no public pick by pick log, and no Watchdog graded record is matched to it.
Is Sharp Football Analysis worth it?

For the money you get Warren Sharp's NFL and college picks with unit sizes, push and email alerts, and, in bigger bundles, props and fantasy content. What is unproven is whether the seller's own records are complete and whether a buyer can get the same lines after picks move the market, and there are no refunds if it goes badly.
